items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1958-12-10
items.q: I know they're around about the same age

ctx.x: Do you remember any other music when you were young, when you were just a child there? Was there any band or dances?

Oh yeah, they had, at my home they had one of the best brass bands in the world. I mean, that country, you understand? They had one band at my home because Pace Unford grandfather took and taught that band. You see? That Day Range band. Magnolia band too. He was one taught son Henry and father. They had a band at Magnolia and one at your town. Oh yeah. Magnolia too, yeah.

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-06-15
items.q: Him and Sonny Henry, Sonny on trombone, Peer on bass. Amos White on trumpet.

ctx.x: Well, I was thinking Harrison and Chris moved here and you moved here. Your brother Sam moved here. Who else moved here and played music? In the city? From down there?
You may see. There must have been some others. You may see. Well, take my son of Henry. He left. He left. Mike Gouldie came in and played.
Who did he play with down there?

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: Pierre, Harrison Bones, Sonny Henry, all them fellas. Good musicians.

ctx.x: Let's see, I thought Sonny played with Chris for a while.

Yeah, Sonny played with Chris for a while. Yeah, Sonny played with Chris for a while. Good while, too. Sonny went with, with, uh, at the Lick with, lived with, uh, Emmis White. Went to Lick, the half-road house, they call it. Wrecked with Emmis White. What kind of house? Eh?
